title: Family Lines of Judah and Simeon
overview: This chapter lists more families from the tribes of Judah and Simeon, naming their towns and trades, and pauses for a short prayer by a man named Jabez and brief accounts of how some clans took new land.

parts.label: Clans of Judah (vv. 1-8)
parts.note: These names tie Judah's families to real towns like Bethlehem and Tekoa, and 'father of' a town often means its founder or leading clan. For readers back from exile in Babylon, lists like this linked them to their roots and their land.

parts.label: Jabez's prayer (vv. 9-10)
parts.note: His name sounds like the Hebrew word for pain, so he asks God to bless him, widen his land, stay with him and keep him from harm so that pain would not mark his life. The text says only that God granted it; later Jewish tradition called him a respected teacher, but the chapter gives no other details.

parts.label: Craftsmen and an Egyptian wife (vv. 11-20)
parts.note: Othniel and Caleb were remembered as heroes from Israel's early days in the land, and one family lived in a valley named for its skilled workers. A man named Mered married Bithiah, a daughter of a Pharaoh (Egypt's king), but the Hebrew here is jumbled and scholars are unsure how these verses fit together or when this happened.

parts.label: Linen workers and potters (vv. 21-23)
parts.note: Some families were known by their trade, weaving fine linen or making pottery, and some potters worked for the king. Verse 22 is hard to translate, and it is unclear what ruling in Moab or the 'ancient records' refers to.

parts.label: Simeon's families and towns (vv. 24-33)
parts.note: Simeon was a smaller tribe that never grew as large as Judah, and its towns lay inside Judah's southern territory. The note that these were their towns 'until David' suggests they were later counted as part of Judah.

parts.label: Simeon takes new land (vv. 34-43)
parts.note: In King Hezekiah's time, growing Simeonite clans looking for pasture found a spacious, quiet land and wiped out the Hamites and Meunites living there, then took it over; later a group killed the last surviving Amalekites, an old enemy people, in the hills of Seir. The text reports this violence plainly and does not stop to judge it.

think: Jabez's name carried his mother's pain from the day he was born; how much do you think the circumstances of our start in life shape who we become?
